"use client"; import { useState } from "react"; import { IconChart, IconEdit, IconLanguage, IconList } from "@rhs-ui/icons"; import { PromptExamples, type PromptExample } from "@rhs-ui/marketing/prompt-examples"; import { Table, TableBody, TableCell, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow } from "@rhs-ui/primitives/table"; const TICKETS = [ { category: "Billing", before: 412, after: 389 }, { category: "Login and access", before: 188, after: 301 }, { category: "Integrations", before: 96, after: 118 }, { category: "Everything else", before: 241, after: 236 }, ]; const EXAMPLES: PromptExample[] = [ { id: "summarise", label: "Summarise", icon: , prompt: "Summarise the attached 12-page supplier contract for our finance team. Flag anything about payment terms or renewal.", answer: ( <>

Here is the short version for finance.

  • Term: 24 months from 1 March 2027, renewing every year unless either side gives 90 days' notice.
  • Payment: net 45 days from invoice, with 2% a month on late amounts.
  • Price changes: capped at inflation plus 2% a year, and only if announced in writing before 1 November.
  • Worth a second look: clause 9.3 lets the supplier suspend service after one missed payment, with no time to put it right.
), note: "Example output, edited for length", }, { id: "draft", label: "Draft", icon: , prompt: "Draft a reply to a customer whose order of three Kestrel chairs arrived with a cracked leg. Warm tone, offer a replacement or a refund, under 120 words.", answer: ( <>

Subject: Your Kestrel chairs, and how we will put this right

Hi Anouk,

I am so sorry the chairs arrived damaged. That is not how we want an order to begin, and the photo you sent makes the problem very clear.

You can choose how we fix it. We can send a replacement chair this week at no cost, or refund the €189 for that chair to the card you paid with. Either way, there is no need to send the cracked one back.

Just reply with which you prefer, and I will arrange it today.

Warm regards, Mila

), note: "Example output, edited for length", }, { id: "analyse", label: "Analyse", icon: , prompt: "Here are last quarter's support tickets by category. What changed, and what should we look at first?", answer: ( <>

Tickets rose from 937 to 1,044. Almost all of the change sits in one category.

Category Q2 Q3 Change {TICKETS.map((row) => { const change = Math.round(((row.after - row.before) / row.before) * 100); return ( {row.category} {row.before} {row.after} {`${change > 0 ? "+" : "−"}${Math.abs(change)}%`} ); })}

Look at login and access first. It grew by 113 tickets, more than the whole net rise of 107, and the new ones mostly mention single sign-on.

), note: "Example output, with the figures from your export", }, { id: "translate", label: "Translate", icon: , prompt: "Translate this onboarding email into German and Dutch. Keep the product names in English.\n\n“Welcome to Kestrel! Your workspace is ready. Invite your team to get started.”", answer: ( <>

Deutsch

Willkommen bei Kestrel! Ihr Workspace ist bereit. Laden Sie Ihr Team ein, um loszulegen.

Nederlands

Welkom bij Kestrel! Je workspace staat klaar. Nodig je team uit om te beginnen.

), }, ]; export default function Demo(): React.JSX.Element { const [message, setMessage] = useState(""); return (

Four written examples, one tab each, with arrow keys between them. The panels share one cell, so the section keeps its height when you change tab. Three answers carry a note; the last has none, so none is shown. Try this prompt calls the handler

setMessage(`Opened the assistant with: “${prompt.split("\n")[0]?.slice(0, 64)}…”. Demo only: nothing is sent.`)} />

{message}
